name: Gottfried Thomasius

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Lutheran Confessional framework of the 19th century

VINIT.justification: The unconditioned divine state prior to the assumption of humanity.

TANCH.justification: The final doctrinal definition that contains the entire mystery of the person of Christ.

AFWD.justification: The directed movement of the divine nature toward the human state.

AREV.justification: The return of the human nature to the full exercise of divine attributes.

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of the states of humiliation and exaltation.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-identical subject who remains the same throughout the change of states.

FSPLIT.justification: The distinction between the relative divine attributes and the immanent divine attributes.

FFUSE.justification: The reunification of the distinct attributes within the single person of the God-man.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative act of laying aside the use of certain attributes.

EVALF.justification: The negative state of finite existence and suffering.

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous presence of divine and human realities in one consciousness.

IFIX.justification: The permanent and unchangeable witness to the historical life of Christ.

phase_3.void_description: The absolute transcendence of God before the economy of salvation.
phase_3.true_description: The active exercise of divine power and glory.
phase_3.false_description: The state of humiliation and the concealment of majesty.
phase_3.both_description: The union of the infinite and the finite in the person of Jesus.

steps.domain_action: The eternal pre-existence of the Logos in the Godhead.
The Logos recognizes its own identity as the second person of the Trinity.
The Logos initiates the movement toward the assumption of human nature.
The divine attributes are distinguished into those essential to Godhead and those relative to the world.
The Logos affirms the retention of immanent attributes such as holiness and love.
The Logos undergoes the self-emptying of relative attributes such as omnipotence and omniscience.
The resulting state holds both the divine subject and the human limitations in a single person.
The attributes are reintegrated into the unified life of the incarnate Christ.
The life of Christ proceeds through the historical stages of growth and ministry.
The specific events of the life of Christ are recorded as historical fact.
The process of exaltation begins as the human nature is glorified.
The completed work of Christ is sealed in the finality of the ascension.
